summary.text: 山 is a pictograph of mountain peaks standing together; its common meaning is “mountain.”

formation.text: 山 is a whole-graph pictograph of mountain peaks, not a compound of separate semantic or phonetic parts. Shang oracle-bone outlines and varied Shang and Western Zhou bronze depictions are described, alongside later listed script forms.

components.text: The whole graph 山 depicts mountain peaks standing together; it is an indivisible pictorial form, not a set of smaller components.

uncertainties.text: The available account does not establish the date or lexical value of the earliest specimen, precise dates for the listed forms, or a continuous graphic development.

senses.text: 山 means a mountain or hill, a landscape sense found in literary use and still in ordinary use. It refers to a high, pointed landform. The earliest attestation and deeper chronology remain unresolved.

limitations.text: The 《合集》96 reading and its proposed gloss about sacrifice to the nine mountains remain tentative. The 《詩經》 examples support landscape use, but the poem’s composition date and earliest physical witness are unresolved. The reviewed evidence establishes no semantic transition.

items.tradition: Shuowen small-seal style, modern vector redraw
items.caption: In this modern small-seal-style redraw, three upright strokes rise from a curved base; the central stroke extends below the two side strokes. It illustrates a later seal-style form of 山, but does not establish a continuous path of graphic change.
items.alt: Three upright strokes rise from a curved base, with the central stroke extending below the side strokes.
items.selection_reason: The redraw clearly shows a later seal-style form and helps readers compare it with the familiar character. Its shape does not establish how the graph changed across earlier stages.
